officialDescription: In-depth investigation in special topics in Operations and Information Management.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open only to doctoral students.

title: Research Methods for Operations and Information Management
officialDescription: Several advanced analytical methods that are relevant to students' areas of research will be studied in depth in this seminar. Topics may include special mathematical programming; complex decision making; linear models; advanced statistical analysis; and stochastic processes.

title: Seminar in Operations Management
officialDescription: Introduces doctoral students to the current research concerns in the field of Operations Management. The course will also acquaint students with the variety of research tools used in the field, enable them to critically evaluate the research of other scholars in the field as well as to develop research skills in identifying potential research problems to be analyzed.

title: Seminar in Management Information Systems
officialDescription: A topic on a significant applied or theoretical aspect of information systems will be chosen. Broadly, these aspects will encompass modeling, design, implementation, testing, and operation of computer information systems, and the implications of information technologies for the organization.

title: Seminar in Operations Research and Optimization
officialDescription: Introduces classical and state-of-the-art optimization methods, modeling techniques, exact algorithms and heuristics, emphasizing deterministic operations research and computational complexity theory.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Instructor consent.

title: Research and Independent Study in Animal Diseases
Microbiology of Atypical Bacteria
officialDescription: An in-depth presentation of current information on medically significant atypical bacteria, with emphasis on molecular aspects of pathogenesis.

title: Viral Pathogenesis
officialDescription: Review and discussion of recent advances regarding mechanisms involved in the development of viral disease at the virus, host, organ, tissue, cell, sub-cellular and molecular levels. Current advances in virus-host interactions will be discussed, including virulence factors, mechanisms of suppression and evasion of host responses, oncogenesis, persistence, immunopathology, neurotropism, neuroinvasion.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: A course in virology or microbiology and one in biochemistry, with consent of the instructor. Recommended preparation: A course in immunology or pathology.

title: Vaccines and Immunotherapeutics
officialDescription: Students develop an understanding of approaches for scientists and engineers to use the immune system to combat infectious and chronic diseases. Both traditional and modern molecular approaches to vaccine and immunotherapy design will be discussed. Students will gain an appreciation for the transition from basic research to practical applications.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PATH 3401 or an equivalent course in immunology.

title: Veterinary Pathology Lecture Series
officialDescription: Lectures on veterinary and comparative anatomic pathology organized by animal species or disease classification utilizing lectures on electronic media in the context of a prescribed plan of study. May be repeated for credit with change in content.

title: Practicum in Veterinary Anatomic Pathology
officialDescription: Service-based learning of veterinary anatomic pathology through gross and histologic evaluation of necropsy and biopsy case material by direct review with faculty pathologists.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open only to veterinarians accepted into the residency program in veterinary pathology.

title: Veterinary Pathology Seminar
officialDescription: Blinded examination of gross and histologic lesions with emphasis on lesion recognition, description and disease diagnosis, followed by group discussion of each case.

title: Immunobiology
officialDescription: Principles of basic and clinical immunobiology; phylogeny and ontogeny of the immune response, characteristics of the immune response, cellular and humoral immunity; central and peripheral lymphoid tissues; mechanisms of immunologic injury and immunologic diseases; comparative and veterinary immunology; transplantation and tumor immunology.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open with consent of instructor to graduate students, upper-level Honors students, and senior undergrad students with recommended preparation. Recommended preparation: Previous coursework in Biochemistry, Genetics, Cell Biology, and Microbiology.

title: Avian Pathology
officialDescription: A comprehensive study of systemic avian pathology, stressing the correlation of pathological changes with clinical and microbiological findings.

title: Molecular Approaches to Disease Diagnosis and Prevention
officialDescription: Molecular aspects of disease, with emphasis on methodologies and strategies for diagnosis, analysis and prophylaxis.

title: Current Veterinary Pathology Literature
officialDescription: Detailed study of current veterinary pathology literature, with particular emphasis on lesions and mechanisms of disease.

title: Vaccines: Mechanisms of Immune Protection
officialDescription: (Also offered as AH 5632.) Focuses on several different approaches to inducing prophylactic immunity in the host. Both traditional and modern molecular approaches to vaccine design will be discussed. In addition, the mechanisms employed by pathogenic microbes to avoid hosts' immune responses will be examined in the context of vaccine design. The students will gain an appreciation for the transition from basic research to practical applications.

title: Independent Study in Pharmaceutical Sciences
officialDescription: This course will provide students the opportunity to explore a variety of topics associated with the field of drug development.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Instructor consent.

title: Dosage Forms I
officialDescription: Introduces the student to the principles of thermodynamics, ionic equilibrium, chemical kinetics and diffusion. Application of these principles to formulation, stability and dissolution of a drug product, and release from the dosage form for optimum therapeutic outcome. Required of entering graduate students in Pharmaceutics who do not have a Pharmacy background as well as those who do not pass the qualifying examination within the first year of the program.

title: Dosage Forms II
officialDescription: Covers the basic principles of the surface and colloid chemistry and rheology, as these relate to the performance of dispersed system dosage forms including colloids, suspensions, emulsions, suppositories, aerosols, ointments, and transdermals. Required of entering graduate students in Pharmaceutics who do not have a Pharmacy background, and those who do not pass the qualifying examination within the first year of the program.

title: Biopharmaceutics and Pharmacokinetics
officialDescription: Basic principles of biopharmaceutics, bioavailability, and pharmacokinetics, including their application to the rational design of both dosage forms and maximally effective dosing regimens. Intended for graduate students who may not have sufficient previous exposure to biopharmaceutics and pharmakokinetics.

title: Current Literature in Pharmaceutics
officialDescription: Designed to familiarize students with current pharmaceutics literature and to educate students in critical peer review in the pharmaceutics literature.

title: Drug Discovery and Development
officialDescription: The processes of new drug development; target identification, drug discovery process, drug candidate evaluation, preclinical toxicity assessment, drug formulation and delivery, clinical trials for safety and efficacy, and FDA regulation on new drug application.

title: Pharmacogenomics and Personalized Medicine
officialDescription: The allied fields of pharmacogenomics and personalized medicine have become areas of intense interest. Each patient responds to drugs and medical treatments in an individualized way, often having to do with underlying genetics. Individual genetic variance often impacts treatment efficacy, pharmaceutical responses, and toxicological adverse events. This course will consider these knowledge areas, which are at the cutting edge of medical advance. Aspects of personalized medicine that go beyond genetics, including the use of patient-matched stem cells will also be discussed.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students or by instructor consent for prepared upper-level undergraduates. Recommended preparation: A basic understanding of genetics is recommended.

title: Seminar in Pharmaceutics
officialDescription: Reports and discussions.

title: Special Problems in Pharmaceutics
officialDescription: Individualized course for students desiring research experience in any of the areas of pharmacy other than the area chosen by the student for thesis research.

title: Special Topics in Pharmaceutics
officialDescription: Includes topics not presently covered in courses which are pertinent to current departmental research and areas of recent development in the literature.

title: Macromolecules in Drug Design
officialDescription: A cooperative presentation of the fundamentals of medicinal chemistry.

title: Chemical Biology and Drug Design
officialDescription: Introduction to the emerging field of chemical biology with a particular focus on the role it plays in understanding cellular signaling, drug design, and drug development.

title: Small Molecule Structure and Function
officialDescription: Small organic molecules continue to be the preeminent form of therapeutic agents. The small molecules that constitute clinically used agents are developed through a highly interdisciplinary process involving chemists, biologists and healthcare workers in a process commonly referred to as drug discovery. The purpose of this course is to provide the student with a broad view of drug properties, drug function and the drug discovery process.

title: Seminar in Medicinal Chemistry
officialDescription: Reports and discussions.

title: Special Problems in Medicinal Chemistry
officialDescription: Individualized course for students desiring research experience in any of the areas of medicinal chemistry other than the area chosen by the student for thesis research.

title: Special Topics in Medicinal Chemistry
officialDescription: Current developments in Medicinal Chemistry. A course for students needing exposure to topics not covered in other department offerings.

title: Current Literature in Pharmaceutical Sciences
officialDescription: Designed to familiarize students with current pharmaceutical sciences literature and to educate students in critical peer review of this literature.

title: Principles of Safety Evaluation
officialDescription: Introduction to toxicologic risk assessment. Fundamentals of dose-response relationships and risk characterization, and their application in the establishment of permissible exposure limits for drugs and other chemicals in the environment or workplace.

title: Advanced Pharmacology I: Basic Principles
officialDescription: Molecular mechanisms of drug action including occupation and rate theories. Characterization of receptors in-situ and in-vitro.

title: Advanced Pharmacology II: Drug Disposition
officialDescription: Drug absorption, distribution, excretion, metabolism, interaction, allergy, resistance, tolerance, idiosyncrasy and toxicity.

title: Toxicology Scholars Colloquium
officialDescription: Reviews, discussions and seminars focused on the research of scientists who have made significant contributions to the science of toxicology.

title: Seminar in Pharmacology and Toxicology
officialDescription: Reports and discussions on journal and review articles and presentation of personal research results.

title: Seminar in Immunology
officialDescription: Reports and discussions.

title: Special Problems in Pharmacology I
officialDescription: Individualized for students desiring research experience in any of the areas of pharmacology.

title: Special Problems in Toxicology
officialDescription: Individualized course for students desiring research experience in any of the areas of toxicology.

title: Special Topics in Pharmacology
officialDescription: Includes topics not presently covered in courses, which are pertinent to current departmental research and areas of recent development in the literature.

title: Special Topics in Toxicology
officialDescription: Basic principles of toxicology as emphasized by recent developments in the biochemical toxicology literature.

title: Introduction to Managed Care Pharmacy
officialDescription: A study of managed care pharmacy within the United States health care system, with emphasis on managed care organization and control, pharmacy benefits design and management, outcomes measurement, pharmacoeconomics, health care provider and client education, benefits plan financing and marketing, and legal issues of managed care pharmacy.

title: Advanced Pharmacy Administration
officialDescription: A study of modern management techniques applicable in terminal drug distribution. Special emphasis is placed upon quantitative methods and the utilization of electronic data processing.

title: Special Topics in Pharmacy Administration
officialDescription: Current developments in Pharmacy Administration. A course for students needing exposure to topics not covered in other Department of Pharmacy Practice offerings.

title: Advanced Biopharmaceutics
officialDescription: Overview of physico-chemical, biopharmaceutic, and physiologic factors controlling the delivery of drug and their sites of action.

title: Freeze Drying of Pharmaceuticals
officialDescription: The science and technology of freeze drying, including fundamentals of heat and mass transfer gas systems, process design considerations, and formulation strategies with emphasis on stabilization of therapeutic proteins.

title: Complex Equilibria
officialDescription: A study of the physico-chemical and mathematical treatment in pharmaceutical systems. Topics center on thermodynamics, activity coefficients, acids and bases, solubility, complexation solubilization and protein binding.

title: Transport Processes
officialDescription: Emphasis is on the application of the laws of diffusion to dissolution, membrane transport and release of drugs from dosage forms.

title: Kinetics and Mechanisms of Drug Degradation and Stability
officialDescription: A study of the kinetics and mechanisms of drug degradation in the solid and liquid states and drug stabilization.

title: Pharmacokinetics
officialDescription: A discussion of absorption, distribution, and clearance mechanisms, and their impact on concentration-time profiles and drug response.

title: Colloid Chemistry and Interfacial Phenomena
officialDescription: Interfacial phenomena, colloid chemistry.

title: Advanced Toxicology
officialDescription: A study of the harmful effects of toxic chemicals on biological systems. Emphasis is on mechanisms of toxicant action and on practical applications of modern techniques to assess toxicity and hazard.

title: Immunotoxicology
officialDescription: Demonstrates the detrimental effects on the immune system and/or inflammatory response, by a variety of physical and chemical xenobiotics. Emphasis is placed on the mechanisms of chemical and drug-induced immunosuppression, autoimmune response, and allergic response.

title: Independent Study for Graduate Students
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Philosophy, others with consent.

title: Seminar in Contemporary Philosophy
officialDescription: An introduction to contemporary philosophers such as Russell, Carnap, Ayer, Quine, Putnam, and Kripke.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Philosophy, others with consent.

title: Seminar in Aesthetics
officialDescription: A consideration of some of the basic problems in aesthetics.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Philosophy, others with consent.

title: Logic
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Philosophy, others with consent.

title: Action Theory
officialDescription: Examination and analysis of the concept of "action" and related concepts such as "agent" and "intention."
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Philosophy, others with consent.

title: Seminar in Moral Philosophy
officialDescription: A discussion and analysis of significant problems in ethical theory.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Philosophy, others with consent.

title: Seminar in the History of Philosophy
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Philosophy, others with consent.

title: Topics in Africana Philosophy
officialDescription: Philosophical problems from across African American philosophy, Afro-Caribbean philosophy, and African philosophy, examined using approaches from Africana analytical, dialectical, existential, feminist, phenomenological, and pragmatist thought. May include a historical focus on ideas from ancient African philosophy. May be repeated for up to nine credits with change in content.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Philosophy and to others with permission.

title: Seminar on Kant
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Philosophy, others with consent.

title: Seminar on Theory of Knowledge
officialDescription: Problems in the foundations and nature of knowledge. A critical study of recent treatments of the problem of mind. Issues such as the mind-body problem, our knowledge of the existence of other minds, the existence of private languages, will be dealt with in detail.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Philosophy, others with consent.

title: Seminar in Philosophy of Mind
officialDescription: A critical study of recent treatments of the problem of mind. Issues such as the mind-body problem, our knowledge of the existence of other minds, the existence of private languages, will be dealt with in detail.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Philosophy, others with consent.

title: Seminar on Metaphysics
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Philosophy, others with consent.

title: Seminar in Philosophy of Language
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Philosophy, others with consent.

title: Seminar in Philosophical Logic
officialDescription: Topics in the philosophies of logic and mathematics. May include completeness results for non-classical logics, higher-order languages and logics, diagonalization, limitative theorems (Tarski, Godel), paradoxes, and formal theories of truth.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to Philosophy Graduate students only, others with permission of instructor.

title: Seminar in Recent Social and Political Philosophy
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Philosophy, others with consent.

title: Philosophical Issues of Race
officialDescription: An examination of philosophical problems, including those in metaphysics and epistemology to those in value theory ranging from aesthetics to ethics and political philosophy in the study of race. Topics include questions of how race is studied in philosophical anthropology, philosophy of freedom, and metacritical questions of the impact of race in how knowledge is produced or understood (such as epistemology).

title: Seminar
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Philosophy, others with consent.

title: Proposal, Prospectus, and Dissertation Writing Seminar
officialDescription: Philosophy students will write and circulate drafts and get feedback on their proposal, prospectus, or dissertation, and practice the presentation of their work. Students working on philosophical theory outside the department are also welcome.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Philosophy; others by instructor consent.

title: Race in the Formation of the Human Sciences
officialDescription: (Also offered as ANTH 5800, LLAS 5800, POLS 5800.) Exploration of how race and the human sciences emerged out of the theological, epistemological, and political upheavals that resulted in the Euromodern world.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Not open for credit to students who have passed PHIL 5380.

title: Independent Study
officialDescription: A special reading course.

title: Research in Physics
officialDescription: Experimental and theoretical research in selected topics in physics.

title: Physics Seminar
officialDescription: The treatment of special topics, primarily by individual readings and reports.

title: Methods of Theoretical Physics
officialDescription: Vector and tensor analysis for science and technology, curvilinear coordinates, linear algebra, functions of complex variables, differential equations, special functions, elements of Green's functions.

title: Theoretical Mechanics
officialDescription: Classical mechanics: Lagrange equations, central force motion, rigid body motions, small oscillations, Hamilton equations, canonical transformation.

title: Electrodynamics I
officialDescription: Differential formulations of electrostatics and magnetostatics, electromagnetic induction. Maxwell equations, electromagnetic waves, application to wave guides, cavities, and dispersive media. Foundations of special relativity.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PHYS 5101 or instructor consent.

title: Electrodynamics II
officialDescription: Maxwell's equations with time dependent sources; radiation from relativistic charged particles; dynamical laws for charged particles; diffraction of electromagnetic waves.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PHYS 5201 and 5301 or instructor consent.

title: Computational Physics
officialDescription: Introduction to computational physics, including programming in C, C++, and Python. Topics include numerical integration of ordinary differential equations, finite differences and stability analysis, numerical solution of partial differential equations (e.g., the Schroedinger and diffusion equations) in more than one dimension, Krylov space methods (e.g., eigensystem solvers and matrix inversion), and Monte Carlo integration. Introductory machine learning and high-performance computing methods may be covered. Writing code to solve current problems from selected areas of physics and astrophysics.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Recommended preparation: Python, C, C++, Unix.

title: Quantum Mechanics I
officialDescription: Mathematical formulation and interpretation of quantum mechanics. Illustrative examples. Hydrogen atom. Dirac ket and bra vectors, matrix methods. Scattering theory.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PHYS 5101 and 5201 or instructor consent.

title: Quantum Mechanics II
officialDescription: Symmetry and angular momentum. Approximation methods for stationary and time-dependent problems, with applications. Relativistic theory of the electron.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PHYS 5401 or instructor consent.

title: Quantum Mechanics III
officialDescription: Occupation number representation, electron gas, Hartree-Fock approximation, correlation energy, superconductivity, perturbation theory, Green's functions, Feynman diagrams.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PHYS 5402 or instructor consent.

title: Statistical Mechanics
officialDescription: Ensembles, distribution function, partition function. Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac distributions, fluctuations, applications to the properties of solids and liquids and to the kinetic theory of gases.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PHYS 5401 or instructor consent.

title: Advanced Topics in Physics I
officialDescription: Selected topics in theoretical and experimental physics.

title: Atomic Physics
officialDescription: Coupling of angular momenta. Hartree-Fock theory of many electron atoms, fine structure and hyperfine structure. Introduction to group theory.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PHYS 5402.

title: Molecular Physics
officialDescription: Heitler-London and molecular orbital theories for diatomic molecules, semi-empirical methods of poly-atomic molecules.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PHYS 6110.

title: Principles of Lasers
officialDescription: The physics of lasers, including optical pumping and stimulated emission, laser rate equations, optical resonators, non-linear optics, the Kerr effect and Faraday rotation. Applications to gas, crystal, glass, liquid, dye, semiconductor, chemical and ultraviolet lasers, Q-switching, mode-locking, and parametric devices.

title: Fundamentals of Solid State Physics I
officialDescription: Crystal structure, phonons, electronic band structure, metals, insulators and semiconductors.

title: Condensed Matter Physics I
officialDescription: Crystal structure; lattice vibrations; electronic band structure of solids; transport theory; basic properties of metals, semi-conductors and insulators; magnetism; super-conductivity.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PHYS 5402.

title: Condensed Matter Physics II
officialDescription: Crystal structure; lattice vibrations; electronic band structure of solids; transport theory; basic properties of metals, semi-conductors and insulators; magnetism; super-conductivity.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PHYS 6211.

title: Nuclei and Particles
officialDescription: Properties of nuclei and particles, conserved quantities, isospin, quark model, Fermi gas model, electroweak interaction, high energy scattering.

title: Quantum Theory of Fields I
officialDescription: Local gauge invariance, Lagranian formulation, Noether currents, spontaneous breakdown of symmetry, Higgs mechanism and superconductivity, canonical quantization, Feynman diagrams, Green's functions.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PHYS 5403.

title: Quantum Theory of Fields II
officialDescription: Topics chosen from the following: Path integral formalism, generating functionals, renormalization, abelian and non-abelian gauge theories (QED and QCD), electroweak theory, solitons, instantons.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PHYS 6341.

title: Stars and Compact Objects
officialDescription: The structure and evolution of stars. Gravitational collapse, hydrostatic equilibrium, novae and shocks, and compact objects with degenerate matter.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Not open for credit to students who have passed PHYS 4710.

title: Galaxies and the Interstellar Medium
officialDescription: Galaxy formation and evolution in the hierarchical expanding Universe. Properties of the interstellar medium, including star formation and radiative transfer; stellar populations, structure, kinematics and dynamics of galaxies.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Recommended preparation: proficiency in calculus. May be taught with PHYS 4720. Not open for credit to students who have passed PHYS 4720.

title: General Relativity
officialDescription: Gravity and the problem of motion from the ancient Greeks to Newton to Einstein. Special relativity. General relativity. Curvature. Classic tests of general relativity. Gravitational waves. Black holes. Newtonian cosmology. Big Bang theory. Inflation. Dark matter. Dark energy. Accelerating universe.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Not open for credit to students who have passed PHYS 4730.

title: Advanced Methods in Astrophysics
officialDescription: Basic principles and techniques of observational and computational astrophysics. Statistical techniques for data analysis and interpretation of astronomical data. Data mining, visualization, and numerical techniques in simulations of astrophysical systems. Includes short research projects using data from observations and/or simulations.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to Physics graduate students; others by permission. Not open for credit to students who have passed PHYS 4740.

title: Design and Analysis of Agricultural Experiments
officialDescription: Design and analysis of experiments commonly conducted in agricultural field, greenhouse, and laboratory research. Emphasis on replicated treatment experiments based on completely random, randomized block, Latin square, split-plot, and split-block designs. Limited coverage of non-replicated treatment observational-type experiments. Statistical analyses performed primarily in SAS (Statistical Analysis System) software. Presentation of summarized data using computer generated graphics from various software packages.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Recommended Preparation: Introductory college-level statistics.

title: Molecular Laboratory Technology
officialDescription: Laboratory technologies for identification and characterization of molecules important for molecular biology research, genetic manipulation and disease diagnosis. Labs will provide hands-on experience performing basic molecular biology techniques, lectures will cover theoretical basis and application.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Not open to students who have passed PLSC 3210.

title: Plant Breeding and Biotechnology
officialDescription: Principles and applications, economic, social and environmental impacts, advantages, potentials and limitations of major traditional and modern plant breeding technologies including crossing/hybridization, polyploidy, mutagenesis, genetic engineering and genome editing.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: One of BIOL 1102, 1108, 1110; MCB 2410; PLSC 3210, 3230, 4210, or instructor consent.

title: Modern and Traditional Plant Breeding Techniques
officialDescription: Hands-on experiments for traditional and modern plant breeding techniques, including artificial crossing/hybridization, polyploidy induction, plant tissue culture and transgenic plant production, and radiation- and genome editing-mediate mutagenesis.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PLSC 5245.

title: Soil Fertility
officialDescription: Factors governing nutrient uptake by plants, fate of nutrients applied to soils, principles and practices in the use of fertilizers and amendments for crop production, laboratory and field studies of social and plant response to applied nutrients.

title: Soil Morphology
officialDescription: Course covers the main components of soil morphology that include horizonation, soil texture, soil color, redoximorphic features, structure and consistence. This includes describing all that can be seen and felt about different soils in the field and learning how to create a standard soil description.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Instructor consent and PLSC 2120, PLSC 2125 or PLSC 1300.

title: Ecology and Control of Weeds
officialDescription: Weed identification. Weed origin and classification. Losses caused by weeds. Weed competition. Weed seed production, dormancy, and germination. Weed growth and development. Weed biology and life cycles. Cultural, mechanical, and biological weed control methods based on ecological principles. Overview of chemical weed control practices and associated environmental and ecological risks.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Not open to students who have passed PLSC 3820.

title: Soil Management, Soil Health, and Climate Change
officialDescription: This course teaches the following knowledge in the agricultural production systems: concept of soil health, measurements of soil health, carbon cycling and its impact on soil health, nitrogen cycling and its impact on soil health, nutrient management in livestock production systems, soil health and climate, plant and soil management practices impact on soil health.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PLSC 1300 or PLSC 2120 or PLSC 3620.

title: Variable Topics in Plant Science
officialDescription: Topics and credits to be published prior to the registration period preceding the semester offerings.

title: Principles of Physiology and Neurobiology
officialDescription: Molecular foundations of physiology and neurobiology. Discussion of classic and emerging literature, experimental design, and research technologies. Topics may include genetics, protein biology, cell structure and function, and neurophysiology.

title: Principles of Physiology and Neurobiology II
officialDescription: Foundations of physiology and neurobiology. Discussion of classic and emerging literature, experimental design, and research technologies. Emphasis on systems physiology.

title: Anatomy and Physiology for Intraoperative Neuromonitoring
officialDescription: Anatomy and physiology of the nervous and musculoskeletal systems.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Recommended preparation: course background in biology.

title: Fundamentals of Intraoperative Neuromonitoring
officialDescription: Overview of intraoperative neuromonitoring. Basics underlying recording of signals and discussion of main neuromonitoring modalities, common surgeries employing neuromonitoring, operating room protocols and procedures.

title: Principles of Applied Intraoperative Neuromonitoring
officialDescription: Components of neuromonitoring machines; guidance on use of equipment, writing and following protocols, recognizing and troubleshooting common sources of noise and artifacts in an operating room setting. Student work will include real case studies that collected during neuromonitoring of surgical procedures.

title: Clinical Practicum in Intraoperative Neuromonitoring
officialDescription: Direct student involvement in intraoperative neuromonitoring of various surgical procedures, observing live signals obtained in a clinical setting, interaction with patients, surgeons and operating room staff, and review of operating room protocols and procedures.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PNB 5101, 5102 and 5103 with an average GPA of 3.0 or higher in these classes, and instructor consent.

title: Seminar in Intraoperative Neuromonitoring
officialDescription: Presentations of clinical and nonclinical topics affecting the daily job of an intraoperative neuromonitoring clinician. Topics may include the sterile field; infection control; needle, electrical, radiation and fire safety; patient privacy laws (HIPAA); professional conduct and communication; and diversity in the workplace.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Instructor consent.

title: Advanced Modalities in Intraoperative Neuromonitoring
officialDescription: Comprehensive didactic and laboratory training on advanced neuromonitoring modalities (tests) such as Phase Reversal, Motor Mapping, D-Wave, Nerve Action Potential and H-Reflex.

title: Clinical Research Methods in Intraoperative Neuromonitoring
officialDescription: Research methods and experimental design in a clinical setting. Common and advanced neurodiagnostic modalities, effects of anesthesia on neurophysiological data, and evaluation of multimodality monitoring. Discussion and critique of published literature, and development of a student generated research proposal.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PNB 5101, 5102 and 5103. Recommended preparation: PNB 5104 and 5105.

title: Cadaver Lab for Intraoperative Neuromonitoring
officialDescription: Hands on laboratory featuring anterior and posterior dissection of bodies from human donors. Emphasis on muscle origins, insertions, innervations, and nerve plexuses.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PNB 5101.

title: Clinical Neuroanatomy
officialDescription: Pathologies of the spinal canal and the nervous system. Presentation of clinical papers and cases, emphasizing patient symptoms and treatments.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Not open for credit to students who have passed PNB 5395 when offered as "Clinical Neuroanatomy."

title: Physiological Signal Transduction: Principles, Pathways, and Applications
officialDescription: Signal transduction and regulation of development in physiological systems. Emphasis on genetic, molecular, and cellular methods; designing and interpreting experiments based upon research developments in current literature.

title: Molecular Endocrinology
officialDescription: Molecular mechanism(s) of hormone action in vertebrates and invertebrates. Molecular and genetic characterization of hormones, receptors, and signal transduction, and hormone actions at the molecular, cellular, and organismal levels. Includes student presentations on selected papers.

title: Electron Microscopy
officialDescription: Lectures and laboratory exercises on the principles and practice of biological electron microscopy.

title: Membrane Transport in Health and Disease
officialDescription: Fundamental mechanisms by which water and small molecules are transported across biological membranes. Biophysical and biochemical analysis of transport by diffusion, osmosis, channels, carriers and pumps in health and disease.

title: Projects in Electron Microscopy
officialDescription: Electron microscopy as a research method in biological sciences.

title: Investigation of Special Topics in Physiology and Neurobiology
officialDescription: Advanced study within Physiology and Neurobiology.

title: Research in Physiology and Neurobiology
officialDescription: Research in Physiology and Neurobiology in pursuit of a graduate degree.

title: Independent Study
officialDescription: Independent investigation of topics in Physiology and Neurobiology.

title: Signal Transduction: Principles, Pathways, and Applications in Physiology
officialDescription: Signal transduction and regulation of development in physiological systems. Emphasis on genetic, molecular, and cellular methods; designing and interpreting experiments based upon research developments in current literature.

title: Seminar in Research and Journal Presentations in Physiology and Neurobiology
officialDescription: Provides the opportunity for graduate students to present journal articles and their laboratory research in physiology and neurobiology to the department.

title: Ion Channels and Physiology
officialDescription: Exploration of major classes of ion channels, including ligand-gated, voltage-gated, mechanosensitive, thermosensitive and light-sensitive channels and their roles in physiology. Discussions of research approaches and emerging technologies in ion channel physiology.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PNB 5001 and 5002.

title: Developmental Neurobiology
officialDescription: Molecular mechanisms of neurodevelopment. Neural induction, cell fate determination, neurogenesis, axon targeting, neuronal migration, synapse formation and activity-dependent synaptic remodeling.

title: Molecular and Cellular Neurobiology
officialDescription: Molecular and cellular aspects of modern neurobiology including the analysis of neuronal proteins and their post-translational modifications, the dynamics of cellular substructures, and various signaling mechanisms in nerve cells including synaptic transmission. Molecular and cellular biology of selected neurological disorders.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to PNB grad students or seniors who have passed PNB 3251, PNB 3275, and one of MCB 2000, 2210, or MCB 3010. Consent of instructor required for non-PNB graduate students.

title: Cells, Synapses, and Circuits
officialDescription: Cellular neurophysiology and circuit neuroscience in multiple systems. Emphasis on applying basic principles of neurophysiology to the study of neural circuit function. Topics covered may include classical and cutting-edge methodologies for deciphering neuronal cell type diversity, cellular and synaptic electrophysiology, neuroanatomy, circuit function and behavior. Student work may include engaging in lectures, critical readings of primary literature, group discussions and presentations.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PNB 5001 or PNB 5002 or instructor consent. Not open for credit to students who have passed PNB 5395 when offered as "Cells, Synapses, and Circuits."

title: Investigation of Special Topics in Political Science
Proseminar in Political Theory
officialDescription: Historical survey and analysis of fundamental concepts in political theory.

title: Political Theory
officialDescription: Historical and conceptual analysis of selected political ideas such as justice, liberty, rights, political obligation, or the state; including an examination of one or more major schools or bodies of political thought from ancient to contemporary times.

title: Theories of Human Rights
officialDescription: Debates about the meaning of human rights and their importance.

title: Decolonial Feminisms
officialDescription: (Also offered as WGSS 5120, NAIS 5120.) Latin American and Latinx feminist political thought addressing imperialism, settler colonialism, and coloniality.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Not open for credit to students who passed WGSS 5395 when offered as "Decolonial Feminism."

title: Democratic Institutions
officialDescription: Rules that structure access to power and policy-making process across countries; changes over time; and major political effects. Topics include the electoral system, presidentialism, government formation, legislative committees, federalism, and the courts.

title: Proseminar in International Relations
officialDescription: Current theories of and methodological approaches to international relations.

title: International Security
officialDescription: Political and military issues as they intersect at the international level, such as war, terrorism, alliances, and intervention.

title: Human Security
officialDescription: Examination of emerging conceptions of human security, important elements of which include good governance, food, water, political, economic, and environmental security. Definition, measurement, and politics of human security. Relationship to domestic and international policy-making and advocacy.

title: International Organization and Law
officialDescription: International cooperation to resolve economic, social, and political transnational problems.

title: Economic Rights
officialDescription: (Also offered as ECON 5128, HRTS 5390.) Explores the conceptual bases, measurement, and policy applications of economic rights. Specific topics will include: child labor, the right to development, non-governmental initiatives, and the institutionalization of economic rights (e.g., constitutionalization versus statutory implementation versus discretionary policies).

title: Special Topics in American Politics
officialDescription: Advanced study of selected topics. Intensive examination of research literature dealing with particular aspects of American politics.

title: American Political Institutions and Policy
officialDescription: The institutions and policy-making process of American government.

title: American Political Behavior
officialDescription: The political behavior of the American public, including public opinion, voting behavior, and other forms of participation.

title: American Race, Gender and Ethnic Politics
officialDescription: (Also offered as WGSS 5409.) The politics of American race, gender and ethnicity, with a focus on disadvantaged groups and their influence on the political process.

title: Black Feminist Theory and Politics
officialDescription: (Also offered as WGSS 5410.) Major debates at the core of black feminist theory, emphasizing the ways in which interlocking systems of oppression uphold and sustain each other in contemporary U.S. politics.

title: Human Rights and Armed Conflict
officialDescription: (Also offered as HRTS 5460.) Examines the relationship between human rights and armed conflict from a social science perspective. Explores human rights abuses as cause and consequence of armed conflict. Evaluates the effectiveness of the human rights and humanitarian approaches to conflict management.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Not open for credit to students who have passed HRTS 3460.

title: Seminar in Public Law
officialDescription: Selected topics in public law, the administration of justice, and jurisprudence.

title: Judicial Decision-Making
officialDescription: The judicial decision-making process in terms of methods and models developed in the framework of the behavioral sciences.

title: Nature of Political Inquiry
officialDescription: The scope of political science, modes of inquiry, the role of concepts and theory. Graduate students are urged to take the course in their first semester.

title: Seminar in Quantitative Methods of Political Science
officialDescription: Introduction to the data analysis techniques most often used by political scientists. Requires no previous background in statistics.

title: Seminar in Qualitative Methods of Political Science
officialDescription: A survey of qualitative research methods. Training in use of case studies, comparative historical approach, interviewing and focus groups, ethnography and interpretive methods.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: POLS 5600 and 5605.

title: Research Design and Development
officialDescription: Introduction to research methods and designs in political science. Students will develop and conduct original research projects. Intended for master’s students in their first semester.

title: Political Science Professional Development
officialDescription: Exploration of careers that involve researching and thinking about politics. Required for 5th Year M.A. students. Does not fulfill Methods or Subfield course requirements for POLS Ph.D. students.

title: Prospectus and Dissertation Writing Seminar
officialDescription: Writing workshop facilitates prospectus and dissertation writing.

title: Political Science Fiction
officialDescription: International relations theory and speculative fiction as interpretations and interrogations of war, peace, politics, knowledge, and imagination.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Not open for credit to students who have passed POLS 3710.

title: Race in the Formation of the Human Sciences
officialDescription: (Also offered as ANTH 5800, LLAS 5800, PHIL 5800.) Exploration of how race and the human sciences emerged out of the theological, epistemological, and political upheavals that resulted in the Euromodern world.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Not open for credit to students who have passed PHIL 5380.

title: Polymer Physics
officialDescription: Modern concepts relating to glassy, rubbery and organized states of bulk polymers. Considers rubber elasticity, glass-to-rubber transitions, networks, elements of crystallization, blends and interfacial phenomena.

title: Polymer Properties
officialDescription: (Also offered as CHEG 5352.) Interrelationships between solid state structure, dynamics, and mechanical properties of non-crystalline and semi-crystalline polymers. Considers polymer viscoelasticity, diffusion, failure mechanism, and elementary polymer rheology.

title: Polymer Rheology
officialDescription: (Also offered as CHEG 5367.) Analysis of the deformation and flow of polymeric materials. Topics include non-Newtonian flow, viscoelastic behavior and melt fracture with application to polymer processing.

title: Polymer Synthesis
officialDescription: (Also offered as CHEM 5380.) Chemistry of the formation of high polymers, including kinetics, mechanisms, and stereochemistry of step growth and addition polymerization. Recent advances in polymer synthesis.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Not open for credit to students who have passed CHEM 5380. (RG5494)

title: Polymer Physical Chemistry
officialDescription: (Also offered as CHEM 5381.) A molecular description of the fundamental physico-chemical aspects of polymer solutions and solids. Considers thermodynamics, chain statistics, dynamics, and structure of polymer molecules.

title: Polymer Characterization I
officialDescription: (Also offered as CHEM 5382.) Experimental techniques for characterizing polymers on a molecular level, with emphasis on the provision of a working knowledge of instrumental analysis. Experiments include dilute solution viscosity, vapor pressure osmometry, gel permeation chromatography, chemical and spectroscopic analysis.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Not open for credit to students who have passed CHEM 5382.(RG5495)

title: Polymer Characterization II
officialDescription: (Also offered as CHEM 5384.) Experimental techniques for characterizing polymers on a macroscopic scale, with emphasis on provision of a working knowledge of instrumental analysis. Experiments include calorimetry, mechanical analysis, surface characterization, and structure determination.

title: Polymer Processing
officialDescription: Various polymer processing techniques: extrusion; injection molding; film and sheet processing; blow molding; thermoforming; fiber spinning; processing of thermosets and special polymers.

title: Nanostructural Characterization
officialDescription: Various types of scattering techniques (diffraction, small angle scattering, reflectometry) to investigate global structure of polymeric or other soft materials ranging from Å to submicron using different probes (X-ray, neutron, light).

title: Seminar in Polymer Science and Engineering
officialDescription: Presentations by invited guest speakers on topics of current interest in various areas of Polymer Science and Engineering.

title: Professional Seminar
officialDescription: Provides executive leadership and executive training opportunities for students in the Master of Public Administration program.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to students in the Master of Public Administration program.

title: Race and Public Policy
officialDescription: Introduction to the public policy process using the salient, crossing-cutting cleavage of race.

title: Public Policy, Diversity, and Inclusion
officialDescription: Overview of how laws and policies related to diversity and inclusion have evolved from equal employment opportunity and affirmative action, to diversity and inclusion. Topics include measurement of racial or gender bias; measurement of "diversity"; policies that organizations used to achieve diversity; policies to maintain diversity and achieve inclusion.

title: Causal Program Evaluation
officialDescription: (Also offered as ECON 5314.) Survey of the statistical methods and tools commonly used to evaluate causal claims about the impact of public policies and programs. This course is a required Master of Public Policy course.

title: Capital Financing and Budgeting
officialDescription: Examination of the municipal bond market, capital budgeting techniques, and related public policy issues.

title: Financial Management for Public Organizations
officialDescription: Management of financial resources in public organizations. Topics include variance analysis, public sector accounting, financial statement analysis, and forecasting.

title: Program Development and Evaluation
officialDescription: Techniques for evaluating and improving organizational performance and the ability to deal with the challenges posed by changing environments. Topics include strategic planning, program development, program implementation, evaluating effectiveness, and performance measurement and improvement.

title: Leading and Governing Nonprofit Organizations
officialDescription: The theory and practice of effective leadership and governance of nonprofit organizations.

title: Grant Writing and Government Contracting
officialDescription: Introduction to writing for private grants and government contracts. Includes responding to requests for proposals for government and nonprofit service provision as well as writing and managing a formal proposal preparation.

title: Labor-Management Relations, Negotiation, and Contract Management
officialDescription: Overview of the fundamentals associated with collective bargaining in the public sector.

title: Public Investment Management
officialDescription: Key dimensions of investment decision making in government, including portfolio analysis and understanding of appropriate investment instruments.

title: Analysis for Management Decision Making
officialDescription: Analytic approaches to decision making in a public management environment.

title: Business Functions of Nonprofit Organizations
officialDescription: Management of financial resources in nonprofit organizations. Topics include variance analysis, nonprofit accounting, financial statement analysis, internal controls, cash management and forecasting.

title: Nonprofit Advocacy, Government Relations, and Law
officialDescription: Legal landscape of nonprofit organizations; theory and application of effective tactics and approaches to advocacy and government relations by nonprofit organizations.

title: Quantitative Methods for Public Policy
officialDescription: Quantitative tools necessary to manage and evaluate public programs.

title: Advanced Quantitative Methods
officialDescription: Advanced statistics for survey research analysis.

title: Nonprofit Marketing and Stakeholder Communications
officialDescription: Approaches for creating effective nonprofit stakeholder communications and marketing plans to promote the mission and service of the organizations.

title: Fund Development and Nonprofit Sustainability
officialDescription: Core elements of developing a fund development (revenue) strategy for nonprofit organizations, including common revenue models, philanthropic models, and earned-income methods for funding organizational sustainability.

title: Economics of Education Reform
officialDescription: (Also offered as EDLR 6322.) Examines a number of prominent education reform strategies, using economics as a lens through which to understand the motivations for and potential impacts of each. Economics enables us to focus on the incentives created by these policies, allowing us to predict their intended and unintended consequences. We will utilize this framework throughout the course as we read about and evaluate the effectiveness of various educational interventions and policy reforms. Topics include (among others): class size reduction, teacher quality and teacher certification, merit pay, school accountability, school choice, school finance reform, early childhood education, and topics in higher education.

title: Introduction to Public Policy and Management
officialDescription: Introduction to the fundamentals of public policy and public management in the United States with a focus on developing the communication skills required in a professional workplace.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open only to MPA and MPP students.

title: Public Opinion and Democratic Processes
officialDescription: American public opinion in the context of democratic theory.

title: Policy Analysis
officialDescription: Approaches and techniques used to evaluate public programs and public policy.

title: Data Analytics with R for Policy and Management
officialDescription: Computational tools and techniques for acquiring, organizing, and visualizing complex data to answer social science research questions using the open-source statistical package R.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Not open for credit to students who have passed PP 5397 when offered as "Data Analytics with R for Policy and Management."

title: Social Policy
officialDescription: Examination of the concepts and principles of public policy analysis, with applications to important social issues.

title: Project Management in the Public Sector
officialDescription: Theory and techniques for successful management of public sector projects. This is a required MPA course.

title: Child and Family Policy
officialDescription: Theory and practice of child and family policy. Topics may include marriage and divorce, fertility, employment, and human capital.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Not open for credit to students who have passed PP 4346.

title: Applied Policy Issues
officialDescription: Overview of important policy issues in the United States and integrates a variety of analytical techniques used in the evaluation of public policies.

title: Urban Planning Principles and Methods
officialDescription: Introduction to the urban planning process, including commonly used planning topics, practices, and tools that planners need to professionally conduct their tasks. Lectures, discussion and simulated planning projects.

title: Public Procurement and Contracting
officialDescription: Principles of contract formulation and administration in public procurement, including practices in procurement activities from the identification of the need through the close out of contract activities; best practices for effective contracting relationships between the public and private and nonprofit sectors.

title: Urban and Regional Policy
officialDescription: Theories and empirical analyses related to urban and regional policy challenges. Students will develop skills in employing analytical frameworks and empirical techniques to investigate urban and regional policy issues.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Recommended preparation: PP 5331 and 5375.

title: Policymaking and Legislation
officialDescription: Introduction to the role and processes of Connecticut’s General Assembly.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Not open for credit to students who have passed PP 4357 or PP 5397 when offered as "Policymaking and Legislation."

title: Crisis Management
officialDescription: Overview of types and characteristics of crises, their impacts and challenges, and strategies for managing them. Topics include emergency management policy and doctrine, incident management systems, individual preparedness, and community resilience.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Recommended preparation: PP 5361.

title: Theory and Management of Public Service Organizations
officialDescription: Core management and behavioral concepts to effectively lead a public organization. Topics include leadership, strategic planning, managing organizational performance, and organizational structure, culture and politics.

title: Local Government Management and Leadership
officialDescription: An examination of the characteristic managerial problems of the several functions of local government such as police, fire, traffic, public works, parks, health, recreation. Designed for individuals planning to work with citizen agencies, in agencies for governmental management, or in journalism.

title: Public Finance and Budgeting
officialDescription: Techniques, practice, and organization of financial functions in governmental organizations, including revenue analysis, budgeting skills, and financial statement analysis.

title: Human Resource Management
officialDescription: The structures, processes, and principles of human resource management and labor-management relations in the public service, and examination of contemporary human resource policies and challenges.

title: Public Service Executive Leadership
officialDescription: Theory and application of tactics and techniques used to enhance effective leadership and strategic management.

title: Performance Management and Accountability
officialDescription: Logic and application of measurement to managing the performance of programs. Topics include performance frameworks, including program logic models and results-based accountability, and performance data visualizations and dashboards.

title: Applied Research Design
officialDescription: Research design for organizational management and policy analysis and evaluation. How to communicate, execute and evaluate research. Skills in selecting appropriate analytic procedures and properly interpreting and reporting results.

title: Capstone Portfolio
officialDescription: Provides a synthesis of basic skills and competencies important for future professionals in the public service. This is a required MPA and MPP course.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open only to MPA and MPP students.

title: Budgeting in Public Service Organizations
officialDescription: Processes and techniques of public budgeting; the principles and roles of budgets in public service organizations; analytic tools, concepts, and principles of budget analysis and decision making.

title: Topics in Financial Management
officialDescription: Synthesizes the lessons in public sector financial management as they apply to the professional practice of the chief financial officer. Combines research literature, expert testimony, professional association position papers, cases, documentaries and discussion in order to expose students to the subject matter and the decision demands of leaders in this field.

title: Economic Analysis for Public Policy and Management
officialDescription: Application of basic microeconomic analysis to public policy and management problems. Required for the MPA and MPP programs.

title: Applied Quantitative Methods
officialDescription: Statistical reasoning, tools, and techniques for effective public management.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open only to students in the Master of Public Administration or the M.A. in Survey Research programs.

title: Qualitative Methods in Public Policy
officialDescription: Development and design of qualitative research.

title: Principles and Methods of Survey Research I
officialDescription: Exploration of the theory and practice of survey research, including sampling, questionnaire design, analysis and reporting results.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open only to Master of Arts in Survey Research or Graduate Certificate in Survey Research students, department consent required.

title: Project Management in Survey Research
officialDescription: This course will explore the application of project management techniques to the management of survey research projects.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Recommended preparation: PP 5379.

title: Principles and Methods of Survey Research II
officialDescription: Advanced exploration of the practice of survey research and questionnaire design.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open only to Master of Arts in Survey Research or Graduate Certificate in Survey Research students, department consent required.

title: Attitude Formation
officialDescription: Theories of attitude formation and attitude change.

title: Survey Research Analysis and Reporting
officialDescription: Analytic writing skills that apply specifically to preparing survey research reports.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Recommended preparation: PP 5376 and PP 5379.

title: Surveys for Market Research
officialDescription: An exploration of how survey research techniques and methods are used to address market research problems.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Recommended preparation: PP 5379.

title: Capstone on the Future of Survey Research
officialDescription: Capstone research on problems and opportunities in the survey research industry for students nearing completion of the Master of Arts in Survey Research program.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Department consent. Recommended preparation: student is in the last or next to last semester of study in the Master of Arts in Survey Research program.

title: Supervised Internship
officialDescription: Experience in a public organization under competent supervision.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open only to students in the Master of Public Administration or the M.A. in Survey Research programs.

title: Foundations of Research in the Psychological Sciences I
officialDescription: Introduction to the logic of experimental design and data analysis in the psychological sciences. Analysis of group designs, especially analysis of variance, and introduction to hypothesis testing.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Psychological Sciences, others with consent.

title: Foundations of Research in the Psychological Sciences II
officialDescription: Expands on material covered in PSYC 5104, including the development and application of correlational methods specific to conducting and understanding research in the psychological sciences.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PSYC 5104; open to graduate students in Psychological Sciences, others by consent.

title: Statistical Analysis of Neural Data
officialDescription: Practical introduction to the analysis of neural data. Lectures and problem sets will involve programming in Matlab, R, or Python. Course is suitable for students with a background in either quantitative methods or neuroscience.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students; advanced undergraduates with instructor consent.

title: First Year Proseminar
officialDescription: The departmental proseminar course, designed specifically for all incoming graduate students, includes faculty presentations from each program, departmental poster night, colloquiums, and a skill set presentation.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Not open for credit to students who have passed PSYC 5170 when offered as Departmental Proseminar.

title: Health Psychology
officialDescription: Interaction of biological, psychological, and social factors in health. Topics include disease prevention and health promotion, psychosocial factors in treatment of illness, and stress and coping processes.

title: Occupational Health Psychology
officialDescription: Introduction to research in occupational health and the field of occupational health psychology in a proseminar format. Topics include work stress, worker participation in hazard management, epidemiology of occupational exposures, workplace incivility, and design of safe work environments.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: STAT 5105 or NURS 5020 or PUBH 5434.

title: Meta Analysis: Theory and Practice
officialDescription: Methods of research synthesis, including the literature review and the place of quantitative methods in drawing conclusions from existing empirical research. Introduces the statistical techniques of meta-analysis, which integrates the results of independent studies addressing the same hypothesis.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: STAT 5105.

title: Foundations in Neuropsychology
officialDescription: An introduction to neuropsychology, including functional neuroanatomy, neurochemistry, neuropharmacology and cognitive/emotional function and dysfunction.

title: Neuropsychological Assessment
officialDescription: An introduction to clinical neuropsychological assessment, including review of neuroanatomy and neuropsychological functions, common syndromes of neuropsychological dysfunction, specific tests to measure neuropsychological functions and professional issues for the neuropsychologist.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PSYC 5140.

title: Neurodevelopment and Plasticity
officialDescription: (Also offered as COGS 5130.) Overview of brain development including embryonic neurogenetics; evolution and evo-devo; how emergent behavioral capabilities reflect neural growth in neurobehavioral development; and how disruptions of neurodevelopment cause developmental disabilities. Offered alternating years in spring semester.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in PSYC, SLHS, PNB; others with consent of instructor.

title: Current Topics in Psychology
officialDescription: Selected topics in psychology are studied with particular attention to recent developments in the field.

title: Special Topics in Cognitive Science
officialDescription: May be repeated for up to 12 credits with change in content.

title: Behavioral Neuroscience Research Seminar
officialDescription: Seminar on current research, with intra- and extra-mural colloquium speakers.

title: Neuropsychopharmacology
officialDescription: Review of the anatomy and physiology of the CNS and then discuss the effects of pharmacological agents on it. Topics include general anesthetics, hypnotics and sedatives, anticonvulsants, alcohol, muscle relaxants, tranquilizers, hallucinogens, and narcotics. Student presentations will treat topics relating the CNS and behavioral pharmacology.

title: Neural Foundations of Learning and Memory
officialDescription: Examination of the processes involved in habituation, conditioning, learning, and memory through a study of the neural elements and systems involved in their production and maintenance.

title: Current Topics in Behavioral Neuroscience
officialDescription: Special problems or areas of research are studied with particular attention to recent developments in the field.

title: Special Topics in Behavioral Neuroscience
officialDescription: May be repeated for credit with a change in topic.

title: Neurobiology of Aging: Changes in Cognitive Processes
officialDescription: Neural basis of age-related changes in learning and memory. Both the normal aging process and age-related pathologies examined. Encompasses both animal models and human data.

title: Research Seminar in Clinical Psychology
officialDescription: Advanced seminar presentations by faculty, graduate students, and visiting speakers on current theoretical developments and empirical research in clinical psychology.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Clinical Psychology and others with consent.

title: Practicum in Interviewing and Cognitive Assessment
officialDescription: An introduction to psychological assessment with supervised practice in administering and interpreting clinical interviews and psychological tests.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Clinical Psychology and others with consent.

title: Adult Psychopathology
officialDescription: Theoretical and descriptive overviews of mental disorder that afflict adults, emphasizing etiology, diagnosis, and conceptualization.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Clinical Psychology and others with consent.

title: Developmental Psychopathology
officialDescription: An examination of diagnosis, etiology, and prognosis in child psychopathology.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Clinical Psychology and others with consent.

title: Practicum in Personality Assessment
officialDescription: Supervised practice in administration and interpretation of clinical tests and case history material, report writing and discussion of implications of diagnostic data for therapeutic procedures.

title: Psychodynamics
officialDescription: Overview of theoretical and empirical literature about theories of personality development and models of behavior change processes.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Clinical Psychology and others with consent.

title: Professional Issues in Clinical Psychology
officialDescription: An examination of the relations among the law, ethical issues, and professional practices of clinical psychologists and of other providers of mental health services.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Clinical Psychology and others with consent.

title: Empirically Supported Therapy
officialDescription: Instruction in and supervised practice of empirically supported therapeutic techniques and treatments.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Clinical Psychology and to others with consent.

title: Methods of Child and Family Therapy in Clinical Psychology
officialDescription: Overview of multiple intervention models for therapy with children and families.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PSYC 5307; open to graduate students in Clinical Psychology.

title: Research Design and Test Construction
officialDescription: Theoretical issues and practical problems in developing valid measures of personality variables and in designing experimental and quasiexperimental research.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Clinical Psychology and others with consent.

title: Current Topics in Clinical Psychology
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Clinical Psychology and others with consent.

title: Clinical Psychology Research Group
officialDescription: Discussion of ongoing research of faculty and graduate students.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open only to graduate students in Clinical Psychology.

title: Research Seminar in Developmental Psychology
officialDescription: Current research in developmental psychology, with intra- and extramural speakers and directed readings.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open only to graduate students in Psychology.

title: Cognitive Development
officialDescription: Current theory and research on children's conceptual development.

title: Cognitive Neuroscience of Language Across the Lifespan
officialDescription: (Also offered as COGS 5150.) The cognitive neuroscience approach to the study of language across the lifespan. Recent advances in neuroimaging techniques such as MRI, ERP, TMS, and fNIRS are combined with classic lesion studies to address the neurobiological bases of typical and atypical language processing.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to Graduate students in PSYC, LING, SLHS; others with consent of instructor.

title: Developmental Cognitive Neuroscience
officialDescription: Survey of current research and methods in developmental cognitive neuroscience, an interdisciplinary scientific field at the boundaries of neuroscience, developmental psychology, and cognitive science.

title: Development of Language and Related Processes
officialDescription: Experimental and descriptive study of the child's language processes, with emphasis on acquisition, structure, meaning, thought, and the influence of verbal processes on nonverbal behavior.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to Psychology graduate students, others with permission.

title: Language Modality, Neural Plasticity, and Development
officialDescription: An integrative approach that reveals the contribution of sign language research to the understanding of human neural plasticity. Diverse research programs and methodologies (e.g., emerging languages, neuroimaging) are combined with behavioral studies (e.g., cognitive psychology) to address the effects of variable language experiences on language development, cognitive development, and neural organization for language.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in PSYC, LING, SLHS; others with consent of Instructor.

title: Neurobiology of Language: Typical and Atypical Cognition and Language Development
officialDescription: (Also offered as COGS 5140.) Survey of current research on language acquisition in developmentally delayed/pathological populations, including but not restricted to Autism, Williams Syndrome, Down Syndrome, and Specific Language Impairment. Examination of what the language delays and deficits reveal about each disorder, the processes of language acquisition, the representation and organization of language, and the biology/neuropsychology/genetics of language.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Prerequisite: Open only to PSYC, LING, and SLHS graduate students; others with consent. Recommended preparation: PSYC 5440 or COGS 5110 or COGS 5120 or COGS 5130 or COGS 5150 or SLHS 5348 or LING 5110. (RG5467).

title: Infancy and the Effects of Early Experience
officialDescription: Data and theory concerning the effects of early experience in infancy on behavioral and physiological development. Cross-species comparisons are emphasized.

title: Social and Personality Development
officialDescription: Fundamental research and theory on social behavior, social cognition, and interpersonal relations in the preschool period (2-6 years) and in middle childhood (6-12 years). Early childhood precursors and consequences in adolescence. Both normative and atypical development.

title: Current Topics in Developmental Psychology
officialDescription: Selected topics in developmental psychology are studied with particular attention to current research and theoretical trends.

title: Research Team in Developmental Psychology
officialDescription: Planning and execution of both individual and collaborative research projects in developmental psychology.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Psychological Sciences, others with consent.

title: Research Seminar in Language and Cognition
officialDescription: May be repeated for up to 12 credits.

title: Memory
officialDescription: Contrasts associationist, cognitive, connectionist, and cognitive neuroscience approaches to issues involving short-term memory, long-term memory, and the representation of knowledge.

title: Event Cognition
officialDescription: An interdisciplinary examination of events as the fundamental unit of cognition. Event cognition and its relation to memory with reference to diverse methodologies in neuroscience, experimental cognition, and computation.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students and advanced undergraduates with instructor consent.

title: Human Neuroimaging
officialDescription: Designed to introduce or deepen knowledge of human neuroimaging methodologies including EEG and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to explore brain structure and function in relation to behavior and cognition.

title: Introduction to Programming Complex Systems
officialDescription: An introduction to programming in Python by exploring a series of complex systems phenomena. Course is open to students with no, intermediate or advanced programming skills. Topics may include selection from dynamical systems, cellular automata, power laws, self-organization, fractals, neural networks, probabilistic grammars, synchronization, among others.

title: Introduction to Nonlinear Dynamics
officialDescription: Basic concepts and methods of nonlinear dynamics systems theory applied to behavioral time-series data.

title: Advanced Nonlinear Dynamics for the Behavioral Sciences
officialDescription: Advanced concepts and methods of nonlinear dynamics systems theory applied to behavioral time-series data.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: PSYC 5553.

title: Dynamics of Language and Cognition
officialDescription: Application of dynamical systems theory to language modeling.

title: Computational Approaches to Language and Mind
officialDescription: Explores the evolution of computational architectures from semantic spaces to transformers, examining how these systems illuminate and challenge theories of human cognition. Considers the ethical and philosophical implications of artificial intelligence for language, intelligence, and mind.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Psychological Sciences, others including undergraduates, with consent. Not open for credit to students who have passed PSYC 5570 when offered as "Computational Approaches to Language and Mind."

title: Cognition
officialDescription: An introduction to theories of human cognition.

title: Psychology of Language
officialDescription: Psychological aspects of linguistic structure, with particular attention to phonology.

title: Current Topics in Cognitive Science
