title: Bayesian Data Analysis
officialDescription: Theory of statistical inference based on Bayes' Theorem: basic probability theory, linear/nonlinear, graphical, and hierarchical models, decision theory, Bayes estimation and hypothesis testing, prior elicitation, Gibbs sampling, the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm, Monte Carlo integration.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: STAT 5585 and 5685; or instructor consent.

title: Linear Models I
officialDescription: Linear and matrix algebra concepts, generalized inverses of matrices, multivariate normal distribution, distributions of quadratic forms in normal random vectors, least squares estimation for full rank and less than full rank linear models, estimation under linear restrictions, testing linear hypotheses.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Statistics, others with permission.

title: Linear Models II
officialDescription: Multiple comparisons, fixed effects linear models, random-effects and mixed-effects models, generalized linear models,variable selections, regularization and sparsity, support vector machines, additive models and Bayesian linear models.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: STAT 5505, 5605, and 5725; open to Ph.D. students who have passed the Ph.D. Qualifying Exam in Statistics; others with permission.

title: Applied Time Series
officialDescription: Introduction to prediction using time-series regression methods with non-seasonal and seasonal data. Smoothing methods for forecasting. Modeling and forecasting using univariate autoregressive moving average models.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Statistics, others with permission.

title: Causal Inference
officialDescription: Introduction to causal inference, the science of drawing conclusions about cause-and-effect relationships from data. Topics include potential outcomes, randomized trials, causal graphical models, observational studies, instrumental variables, mediation and interference.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Recommended preparation: Familiarity with probability theory and statistical inference; experience with R. Not open for credit to students who have passed STAT 5095 when offered as "Casual Inference."

title: Applied Spatio-Temporal Statistics
officialDescription: Applied statistical methodology and computing for spatio-temporal data, including visualization, models, and inferences. Extreme value analysis in spatio-temporal contexts. Focus on models that account for spatio-temporal dependence and inferences that provide appropriate uncertainty measures, with applications to real-world problems using open-source software.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Statistics, others with permission. Recommended preparation: STAT 5405 or 5605 or GSCU 5400 or 5410 or ERTH 5150 or equivalent.

title: Deep Learning
officialDescription: Foundations of modern deep learning including the statistical learning framework, optimization and gradient descent, and various learning algorithms such as multi-layer perceptrons, convolutional neural networks, transformers, and more.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: STAT 5545 and STAT 5505; or instructor consent. Not open for credit to students who have passed STAT 5095 when offered as "Deep Learning."

title: Statistical Data Science in Action
officialDescription: Real-world statistical data science practice: problem formulation; integration of statistics, computing, and domain knowledge; collaboration; communication; reproducibility; project management.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: STAT 5405 or instructor consent.

title: Statistical Inference I
officialDescription: Exponential families, sufficient statistics, loss function, decision rules, convexity, prior information, unbiasedness, Bayesian analysis, minimaxity, admissibility, simultaneous and shrinkage estimation, invariance, equivariant estimation.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to Ph.D. students who have passed the Ph.D. Qualifying Exam in Statistics, others with permission.

title: Advanced Probability
officialDescription: Fundamentals of measure and integration theory: fields, o-fields, and measures; extension of measures; Lebesgue-Stieltjes measures and distribution functions; measurable functions and integration theorems; the Radon-Nikodym Theorem, product measures, and Fubini's Theorem. Introduction to measure-theoretic probability: probability spaces and random variables; expectation and moments; independence, conditioning, the Borel-Cantelli Lemmas, and other topics as time allows.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to Ph.D. students who have passed the Ph.D. Qualifying Exam in Statistics, others with permission.

title: Seminar in Biostatistics
officialDescription: May be repeated for a total of 24 credits.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Biostatistics, others with permission.

title: Statistical Inference II
officialDescription: Statistics and subfields, conditional expectations and probability distributions, uniformly most powerful tests, uniformly most powerful unbiased tests, confidence sets, conditional inference, robustness, change point problems, order restricted inference, asymptotics of likelihood ratio tests.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: STAT 6315; open to Ph.D. students who have passed the Ph.D. Qualifying Exam in Statistics, others with permission.

title: Statistical Learning and Optimization
officialDescription: (Also offered as BIST 6615.) Computationally intensive statistical learning methods with optimization techniques: classification, discriminant analysis, (generalized) additive models, boosting, regression trees, regularized regression, principal components, support vector machines, and (deep) neural networks.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Instructor consent and intermediate courses in mathematical and applied statistics.

title: Seminar in the Theory of Probability and Stochastic Processes
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in Statistics, others with permission.

title: Special Topics
officialDescription: With a change in topic, may be repeated for a maximum of six credits.

title: Literary Translation: Theory and Practice
officialDescription: A study of the theoretical and practical aspects of literary translation. Translating literature from various genres. May be repeated for a maximum of nine credits with a change of topic.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Six credits of upper division coursework 3000-level or higher in a foreign language or the equivalent.

title: Literary Translation Seminar
officialDescription: Translating literature and studying the practical aspects of the craft of literary translation. May be repeated for a maximum of nine credits with a change of topic.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Six credits of upper division coursework 3000-level or higher in a foreign language or the equivalent.

title: Portfolio Translation Seminar
officialDescription: Translation of literature of any genre or period into English, working toward a final publishable text. Includes preparation of a conference-length paper related to translation theory or practice.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: TRST 5310 and 5311.

title: Decolonial Feminisms
officialDescription: (Also offered as NAIS 5120, POLS 5120.) Latin American and Latinx feminist political thought addressing imperialism, settler colonialism, and coloniality.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Not open for credit to students who passed WGSS 5395 when offered as "Decolonial Feminism."

title: Gender and Culture
officialDescription: (Also offered as ANTH 5315.) Anthropological perspectives on the analysis of gender with special focus on dynamics of gender, culture, and power.

title: Professional Development and Praxis Seminar
officialDescription: Professional orientation in the field of WGSS and potential future workplaces. Topics include starting an MA project, advice on mentoring and networking, preparing for the job market, and confronting institutional barriers to diversity, inclusion, and social justice.

title: Critical Epistemologies and Methodologies
officialDescription: Theoretical underpinnings of critical methodologies and interdisciplinary research including feminist, queer, trans, critical race, post-colonial, indigenous and disability studies. Contemporary debates and ethical dilemmas faced by researchers using critical feminist, interdisciplinary and intersectional epistemologies. Guided experience in designing and producing feminist scholarship.

title: Critical Pedagogies
officialDescription: Overview of critical pedagogical epistemologies and classroom tools for use in interdisciplinary feminist, queer, trans, critical race, indigenous, and disability studies classrooms.

title: MA Capstone
officialDescription: A collaborative seminar focused on supporting students in completing their MA project. Opportunity to reflect on the WGSS knowledge and skills learned and future goals.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Instructor consent. Recommended preparation: WGSS 5365.

title: Special Topics Seminar in Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies
officialDescription: Topics of current interest from a feminist perspective.

title: Variable Topics in Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies
officialDescription: With a change in topics, may be repeated for credit.

title: American Race, Gender and Ethnic Politics
officialDescription: (Also offered as POLS 5409.) The politics of American race, gender and ethnicity, with a focus on disadvantaged groups and their influence on the political process.

title: Black Feminist Theory and Politics
officialDescription: (Also offered as POLS 5410.) Major debates at the core of black feminist theory, emphasizing the ways in which interlocking systems of oppression uphold and sustain each other in contemporary U.S. politics.

title: Topics in the History of American Women
officialDescription: (Also offered as HIST 5555.) May be repeated for a total of 9 credits. Formerly offered as WGSS 5333.

title: Theories of Intersectionality
officialDescription: (Also offered as SOCI 5613.) Analyses of theories that simultaneously take into account dynamics of race, class, gender, sexuality, nation, ability, and other dimensions of social inequality and difference. How scholars research intersectionality, the limits and possibilities of different approaches, and the types of methodologies that are most effective for intersectional analysis.

title: Sexual Citizenship
officialDescription: (Also offered as SOCI 5614.) Sexuality as an axis of citizenship in diverse national and international contexts. Analysis of access to citizenship, relationship recognition, marriage rights, heteronormativity and compulsory heterosexuality, trans citizenship claims, immigration, asylum, sex work, reproductive rights, sex education, racism and racialization, colonialism, and social justice.

title: Feminist Approaches to Disability, Illness, and Care
officialDescription: An examination of care and caregiving across different threads of feminist scholarship in sociology, science and technology studies (STS), and disability studies. Key topics include how care is raced and gendered, disability as an axis of inequality, and how approaches to care have evolved, particularly in feminist disability studies/disability justice.
